The Council authorized Member States to form and deploy a Multinational Security Support mission in close cooperation with Haiti's Government under Chapter VII. This mandate, established in S/RES/2699 (2023), carries a twelve-month term from adoption with a review scheduled for nine months thereafter. [MANDATE]

Funding and support would come from voluntary contributions by individual Member States and regional organizations. The Council called on the mission to establish oversight to prevent human rights violations or abuses, noting that applicable international human rights law applies. [SAFEGUARDS]

China urged caution on Chapter VII citing sovereignty and non-interference. It demanded close consultation between mission leaders and Haiti to secure public support. China called for a broadly agreed political transition, a credible timetable, and engagement with CARICOM and BINUH mediation. [CHINA]
